post.caption: Gold earrings cheaper than a sandwich. Ratners Group was a British jewelry chain that owned Ernest Jones in Britain and Kay Jewelers in America. In 1991 its boss, Gerald Ratner, gave a speech at the Royal Albert Hall in London. He said the group's gold earrings were cheaper than a prawn sandwich, and that they probably would not outlast it. He has said it was meant as a joke. About 500 million pounds then vanished from the group's value. The group was renamed Signet in 1993. Signet bought Zales in 2014 and still owns Kay Jewelers.
